chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about saying tasbīḥ in the place of relieving oneself and reciting the Qur'an.
So he said: "No concession was given in the toilet for more than Āyat al-Kursī; and he may praise Allah, or [recite] a verse."

key_terms.آيَةِ الْكُرْسِيِّ: the Verse of the Throne, recited here as an allowed exception
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: glorifying Allah through prescribed words of praise

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the Qur'an or saying tasbīḥ in the toilet according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on dhikr and Qur'an recitation in the place of relieving oneself. It indicates that recitation there is restricted, with allowance mentioned for Āyat al-Kursī, praising Allah, or a single verse.
